correctness.rationale: For each chord length ℓ(t), integrate s and s² over interval [−λℓ,(1−λ)ℓ] and subtract the u-centroid to obtain I_u=M3/12+h²(M3−M2²/A), h=1/2−λ. The v-marginal is unchanged, contributing A Var(v·X). Triangle chords form two-sided linear tents of width w, yielding M2=4A²/(3w), M3=2A³/w², so the chord coefficient is (1/6+2h²/9)A³/w². The width w is the support function of T−T and reciprocal radial function of its polar; the polar difference hexagon of the standard right triangle has area 3. Affine covariance gives |(T−T)°|=3/(2A), hence angular mean 1/w²=3/(2π A), while mean v-centroidal variance is I/(2A). This yields the exact expectation. For triangle sides a,b,c, I=A(a²+b²+c²)/36 and the Heron/Weitzenböck identity implies I≥A²√3/9 with equality only equilateral. Substituting gives the sharp λ bound and equality, and arbitrarily slender fixed-area triangles exhibit strict contraction below the threshold. Independent 100,000-angle quadrature for three noncongruent triangles verified the inverse-width identity and λ=0.3 response; exact analytic averaging, not samples, proves all cases.
